body:
The most optimal behavior is almost always to have `createImageBitmap` do the absolute minimum processing. E.g, for images, it should keep them in their YUV[A] format, and then do color conversion and alpha multiplication in the same copy operation that does `copyExternalImageToTexture`. In general I am against the idea of trying to specify `ImageBitmapOptions` to try to avoid future color conversion or alpha operations. The entire API was misguided and fragile (and was written to target CPU-based 2D canvas implementations).

I would like for Chromium to completely ignore the `premultiplyAlpha` flag in `ImageBitmapOptions` in terms of the actual pixels stored. Unfortunately it is needed to ensure compliance with [this bad WebGL API choice](https://registry.khronos.org/webgl/specs/latest/1.0/#PIXEL_STORAGE_PARAMETERS), where `ImageBitmap` gets special treatment.

For `colorSpaceConversion`, it is useful in WebGL and WebGPU to have the option to just say "I want the raw pixel values, please pretend the color profile wasn't present".

That's all a big wind-up for saying "I don't think this should be exposed any further, because it was almost-all a bad idea". WebGPU didn't make the same mistake that WebGL did in terms of "`ImageBitmap` is special and ignores alpha and color parameters". In terms of removing the need for these parameters, I'd rather fix that problem by adding a `UNPACK_PREMULTIPLY_ALPHA_BUT_FOR_REAL_WEBGL` enum to un-opt-out `ImageBitmap`.

@ccameron-chromium what is your concrete suggestion on the WebGL API side? At the time the [premultiplyAlpha](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Window/createImageBitmap#premultiplyalpha) option to `createImageBitmap` was specified, all browser implementations were decoding input images to RGBA at the time `ImageBitmap` was created, and multiplying the alpha channel into the color channels. Many developers needed the alpha channel not multiplied in to the color channels, so to avoid a synchronous re-decode during upload of the `ImageBitmap` to a WebGL texture, it was necessary to specify the intent of the `ImageBitmap`.

I have minimal WebGPU experience but https://gpuweb.github.io/gpuweb/#gpucopyexternalimagesourceinfo doesn't allow specifying of any alpha-premultiplication behavior, so for ImageBitmaps at least, it has the same behavior as WebGL - it will obey the `premultiplyAlpha` flag from `ImageBitmap` creation time.

> all browser implementations were decoding input images to RGBA at the time `ImageBitmap` was created, and multiplying the alpha channel into the color channels

Yeah, things sort of solidified around an implementation at a particular moment in time. More than WebGL, it's that things were solidified around un-accelerated 2D canvas implementations.

I think the mistake was having `texImage` from an `ImageBitmap` ignore the unpack state entirely (rather than have a "match" between unpack state and `ImageBitmapOptions` be a "fast path").

IIUC, WebGPU does this correctly. In particular, [here](https://gpuweb.github.io/gpuweb/#gpucopyexternalimagedestinfo) it says "if premultipliedAlpha matches the source image, conversion may not be necessary". So we never ignore the unpack state, but if we created the `ImageBitmap` in a way that matches the unpack state, we can avoid extra conversions.

> what is your concrete suggestion on the WebGL API side?

In the [pixel storage parameters section](https://registry.khronos.org/webgl/specs/latest/1.0/#PIXEL_STORAGE_PARAMETERS), where it say

> If the TexImageSource is an ImageBitmap, then these three parameters will be ignored. Instead the equivalent ImageBitmapOptions should be used to create an ImageBitmap with the desired format.

This is where we hit the problem. Ideally they're not ignored. The remedy that I would suggest, avoiding compatibility issues, would be to add a `UNPACK_IMAGE_BITMAP_EXEMPT_WEBGL` piece of state, which is initially `TRUE` and change the text to be:

> If the TexImageSource is an ImageBitmap and if `UNPACK_IMAGE_BITMAP_EXEMPT_WEBGL` is `TRUE`, then these three parameters will be ignored. Instead the equivalent ImageBitmapOptions should be used to create an ImageBitmap with the desired format.

That way, an application can opt out of this behavior.

@ccameron-chromium 
Thank you.

I apologize for talking about Deno's internal implementation, for example, we currently `createImageBitmap` decodes a 1x1 RGBA8 image (Blob) and stores this as [[[BitmapData]]](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/imagebitmap-and-animations.html#concept-imagebitmap-bitmap-data), which would be expressed in JavaScript as a `Uint8Array([255,0,0,255])`.
According to your answer, it seems that `[[BitmapData]]` should not be decoded in this way?
Would it be appropriate to store informations to `[[BitmapData]]` that things like the ICC Profile contained in the Blob and then apply the conversion at a stage related to actual drawing, such as with `CanvasRenderingContext` or `copyExternalImageToTexture`?

> Would it be appropriate to store informations to `[[BitmapData]]` that things like the ICC Profile contained in the Blob and then apply the conversion at a stage related to actual drawing, such as with `CanvasRenderingContext` or `copyExternalImageToTexture`?

Yes, this is the approach that we have mostly moved to. We decode content to get the pixel values, and we keep its metadata (ICC profile, etc) around.

Conversions are performed only-the-fly during draw. This is usually free (in terms of power and performance) when performed on a GPU. For CPU based drawing systems, more elaborate caching (and maybe even predictive pre-conversion) schemes are necessary.

@whatwg/canvas

I listed the problems with the current specification below that based on the information I received about the current implementation example.

- it is natural to read it as if the image conversion is immediate when you just read the `createImageBitmap` specification
- the use cases have expanded since the API was first designed, and there is an API like [GPUQueue.copyExternalImageToTexture](https://gpuweb.github.io/gpuweb/#dom-gpuqueue-copyexternalimagetotexture) that implicitly expect meta information from the image source

So what I propose this time is to make it clear that
"images will not be converted immediately and user agent will convert on-the-fly that any chance that is required, such as during draw for steps 9 and 10 (if needed also 8)"
starting with `The createImageBitmap(image, options) and createImageBitmap(image, sx, sy, sw, sh, options) methods, when invoked, must run these steps:`.

This change is expected to have the following benefits.

- user agent can optimize performance depending on the rendering target, such as the CPU or GPU
- it will conform to the specifications expected by other APIs that rely on ImageBitmap

On the other hand, not converting the image immediately means that what is stored internally may not be considered bitmap data. Along with this, it may be more appropriate to express the internal slot `[[BitmapData]]` as `[[RawData]]`.

In addition, to perform image conversion on-the-fly, the image conversion options specified in `createImageBitmap` must be stored internally. Would it be better to explicitly state that these options are stored internally? Or would it be better to make it implicitly implementation-oriented?

This change does not change the interface, but it is desirable not to create unintentional changes for API users.

This is a corner case, but for an example, `createImageBitmap` can take an `ImageBitmap` as an argument, so it is possible to apply image conversion to the same image source multiple times. So, there is the last option specified will appear at render target because of the conversion is not performed immediately.

If this change affects existing implementations or other specifications, or if you have any concerns, please point out.
